checks: Desktop starts in centered, tilted overview with minimap and no manual tongue control
Ten simulated seconds idle cannot start battle or allow rivals to ambush the player
Moving into the first swarm collects flies automatically and enters safe shooting practice
C switches to lower side third-person; aiming leaves the camera heading stable
Actual mouse firing spends fly ammunition and starts the five-second warning
Warning is not skipped; pause freezes simulation and audio, and resume completes countdown
A brief Q tap works with no ammunition and pushes a normal opponent away without instant KO
Real mouse-aimed projectiles finish a dizzy opponent from beyond kick range
Owned catapult mounts with E, previews mouse aim, fires on click, preserves fly ammo, reloads and dismounts
Save/reload retains ammunition and battle phase
Portrait phone: visible controls and map fit without overlapping or scrolling
Actual left-stick movement enters a swarm and refills without a collection button
Analog tilt preserves intensity; changing direction steers mid-hop and turns the visible frog
Two simultaneous fingers move and deliberately aim; the inner ring does not fire
Outer ring fires while moving; releasing aim alone restores movement-facing and stops fire
Touch camera toggle changes once per tap and keeps the player inside portrait framing
Contextual mobile kick accepts a short tap against an active opponent with an empty mouth
Portrait catapult controls: visible controls and map fit without overlapping or scrolling
Mobile catapult reuses right-stick hold/drag/release, shows arc and landing marker, and preserves flies
Landscape phone: visible controls and map fit without overlapping or scrolling
Pause clears both touch controls and audio; controls recover after resume and rotation
No uncaught browser runtime errors in desktop or touch flows
limitations: Chromium desktop and CDP touch emulation, not a physical iPhone or Android.
Input is dispatched through real browser handlers. Long simulations use the production model test hook with the live input handler; real WebGL frames and screenshots are rendered at checkpoints.
Software-rendered browser verification does not measure real-device FPS.
